title: Company-wide policies and processes — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview:

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. The goal is to provide a single reference for policy owners, approvers, and employees to ensure consistent compliance, reduce operational friction, and accelerate onboarding.

Owners and scope:
- People Ops: travel policy, expense approvals, internal templates, role-based access review cadence.
- Security & Compliance: access controls, RBAC standards, data classification, audit logging requirements.
- Eng Infra / Eng SRE: change management for infra and production services, release windows, emergency change process.
- Finance & Legal: procurement, vendor contracting, payment approvals, retention of vendor documentation.

1) Access and permissions (RBAC, onboarding/offboarding, least privilege)

Intro:
Redwood enforces role-based access control (RBAC) across cloud accounts, the Redwood control plane, internal tools (PagerDuty, GitHub, Datadog, GCP/AWS/Azure), and third-party SaaS. Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed regularly.

Key controls:
- Roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Read-only. Each service must publish a role mapping document in the service's team wiki.
- Just-in-time access: For elevated, time-limited admin access use the approved JIT workflow (see section below).
- Onboarding: People Ops issues initial access checklist; team leads request additional permissions via the Access Request form (link in templates).
- Offboarding: People Ops triggers immediate revoke for cloud and critical systems; teams must confirm service account rotation where applicable.
- Quarterly access review: Team leads must complete the Access Review spreadsheet by the 10th business day after quarter close. Security runs cross-team reconciliation and escalates exceptions.

Just-in-time (JIT) elevated access procedure:
1. Engineer submits Access Request via Lookup Form (link).
2. Team lead approves for max 8 hours.
3. Security issues temporary credentials through the JIT system; actions are logged.
4. Post-incident, engineer files a short access justification in the team retrospective.

2) Change management (infra, platform, product)

Policy summary:
All production-impacting changes must follow the change management workflow. Non-production changes should follow lightweight approvals documented in team runbooks. Exceptions: emergency fixes with immediate mitigation and post-facto review.

Change types and requirements:
| Change type | Approval required | Testing required | Schedule window | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Routine infra patch | Team lead | Unit + canary staging | Any, small risk | Infra team |
| Production deployment (major) | Eng manager + SRE oncall | Integration + canary + perf test | Approved deploy window | Service owner |
| Emergency change | PagerDuty oncall escalation | Post-deploy rollback plan | ASAP with notification | Oncall engineer |

Standard workflow (non-emergency):
1. Create a change ticket in Jira with description, rollback plan, test plan, and SLO impact.
2. Assign approvers (service owner + SRE).
3. Complete testing in staging and run the perf checklist.
4. Schedule deploy in the approved window and notify stakeholders.
5. Post-deploy verification and close the change ticket.

Rollback and postmortem:
- All production rollbacks must be executed with the SRE oncall present.
- Postmortem required for any rollback that causes >5% user impact or extends >2 hours.

3) Data management (classification, retention, access, backups)

Classification:
- Public: safe for external distribution.
- Internal: company-internal, non-sensitive.
- Confidential: contains PII, customer data, or contractual restrictions.

Storage and access rules:
- Confidential data must be stored in approved systems (encrypted at rest and in transit) and access controlled via IAM groups.
- Production backups are retained for 90 days by default; extended retention requires approval by Security + Legal.
- Data exports: any export of confidential data requires a Data Export Request form and a recipient and retention plan.

Audit & logging:
- Audit logs for privileged actions (IAM changes, key rotations, data exports) must be retained for 1 year in immutable storage.
- Security runs quarterly audits and reports exceptions to the Risk Committee.

Data incident response:
1. Notify Security incident channel and follow the Incident Response playbook.
2. Contain, preserve logs, and engage Legal for breach assessment.
3. Notify affected customers per contractual requirements.

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
- <$5k: Team lead approval.
- $5k–$50k: Dept head + Finance.
- >$50k: VP + Finance + Legal review.

Process steps for purchasing:
1. Create a Purchase Request in procurement system with business justification and budget code.
2. Attach vendor quote and statement of work (if applicable).
3. Route for approvals per matrix.
4. Finance issues PO and coordinates payment.

Expenses & travel reimbursement:
- Employees submit expenses in Concur within 30 days; receipts required for all items >$25.
- Carded purchases must be reconciled weekly by card owners.
- Per diem rules follow the Travel Policy section below.

5) Vendor management and contracting

Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Business sponsor identified.
- Security questionnaire completed (standard vendor security questionnaire).
- Contract reviewed by Legal (include data processing addendum if vendor will process customer data).
- Finance sets payment terms and PO if required.

Vendor risk tiers and controls:
- Tier 1 (High risk): vendors with access to customer data or critical infrastructure. Require SOC2/ISO attestation, yearly security review, and quarterly technical checks.
- Tier 2 (Medium): vendors supporting internal productivity with no access to customer data. Require annual questionnaire.
- Tier 3 (Low): standard SaaS with limited access; annual vendor inventory only.

Offboarding vendors:
- Ensure revocation of all credentials, retrieval of data, and contract termination clauses processed. Preserve vendor invoices and contracts for 7 years per Finance retention policy.

6) Travel policy (business travel, approvals, safety)

Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be booked via the corporate travel portal when possible.
- Manager approval required for international travel and for trips >3 nights.

Expense limits and guidelines:
- Economy or economy-plus for flights under 6 hours; premium economy allowed with manager pre-approval.
- Hotel stays should optimize for safety and proximity; follow per-night cap in the travel portal by city.
- Ground transportation: prefer rideshare or company car services when available.

Safety and emergency contacts:
- Employees must register travel (dates and destination) in the travel portal for health & safety notifications.
- People Ops maintains an emergency contact and will coordinate evacuations if necessary.

7) Internal templates and forms (links and required fields)

This section centralizes company templates. Use the canonical template repository (link in team wiki). Key templates include:
- Access Request form (required fields: requester, justification, systems, duration, approver).
- Purchase Request template (vendor, amount, budget code, justification, approver).
- Data Export Request (dataset, reason, recipient, retention).
- Change Request checklist (description, rollback, testing, approvers).
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (to be completed by vendor and reviewed by Security).

Governance and review cadence:
- Policies are reviewed annually by the owning team. Major changes require cross-functional review and a 14-day comment window.
- Exceptions must be documented and time-boxed; Security and People Ops must approve exceptions to access or retention rules.

Appendix: key contacts and SLAs
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (onboarding, travel, templates)
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.ai (access reviews, audits)
- Finance: procurement@redwood.ai (POs, invoices)
- Eng SRE: oncall@redwood.ai (change approvals, emergency changes)

SLA summary:
- Access request turnaround: 48 business hours for standard requests; JIT for elevated within 4 hours during workday.
- Procurement approvals: <$5k within 5 business days; >$5k typical cadence 10–15 business days.
- Vendor security review: Tier 1 vendors within 15 business days.

Related references:
- See Security "RBAC and Auth" and "Audit logging" pages for technical mappings and IAM group names.
- Change management runbook in eng-platform/runbooks for deployment checklists.
